scorecards.inningsCommentary: Pakistan commenced their first innings at Dubai International Cricket Stadium, aiming to set an imposing baseline total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 147 from Haris Sohail, complemented by a commanding 186-run stand between Haris Sohail and Babar Azam that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.5 RPO. Colin Grandhomme (2/44) maintained tight lines for New Zealand, creating intermittent chances in an otherwise demanding fielding effort. Finishing at 418/5 (166.6 ov), Pakistan established an overwhelming first-innings foundation that firmly dictated the terms of the match.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Dubai International Cricket Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as Pakistan posted 418/5 (166.6 ov) in their opening innings. In response, New Zealand countered with 90/10 (35.3 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 9-Wicket Spell: Yasir Shah (9/41), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Yasir Shah delivered a masterclass for Pakistan (15 Wickets), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Pakistan 63%) and allowing Pakistan to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, New Zealand faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Pakistan's bowling unit, bolstered by Haris Sohail (147 Runs), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Pakistan won by innings & 16 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Pakistan's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While New Zealand produced fighting phases, Pakistan won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
